docs/architecture.md:248:`ViewerPanes` owns four card slots and a detail slot as immutable lifetime snapshots, exposed through `useSyncExternalStore`. Detail transfers the selected preview identity at full scale; Back creates fresh cards while the preceding detail fades until deletion. `ViewerFades` owns the source incoming/outgoing/delete queues, signed8.8 alpha assignments and forward-splice ordering. The retained React layer hooks paint opacity through refs without per-frame React renders. Dismissed confirmation artwork loses its independent preview immediately while its shell fades; browser input/focus cleanup remains separate from core queue flags.
docs/architecture.md:258:`core/viewer-highlights.ts` separates persistent card-slot line/glow latches from replaceable preview identity and caution alpha. Its frame step receives hit booleans and an activity flag; it owns no pointer sampling, DOM or renderer. Warning eligibility reuses `tankLoadEligibility`, retaining active-level capacity and authoritative unlock lists. Alpha assignments use the existing signed8.8 display setter. Browser sampling, warning geometry and preview filters follow in separate slices.
docs/fidelity.md:277:- NaN width/height assignments leave authored scale intact in the primary [Ruffle0.7.1 DisplayObject setters](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/v0.7.1/core/src/avm2/globals/flash/display/display_object.rs#L95), rather than hiding the clip or substituting gameplay radius. The native renderer follows that behavior. Procedural mock bounds feed the same record-selection algorithm; headless simulation defaults use stored-radius estimates until a geometry provider is bound. No original artwork or paths were added.
docs/fidelity.md:298:- Main position setters truncate to twentieth-pixel twips after each assignment; alpha setters truncate to8.8 fixed point. This follows the reference runtime's [DisplayObject wrappers](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/v0.7.1/core/src/avm2/globals/flash/display/display_object.rs#L314), [Twips conversion](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/v0.7.1/swf/src/types/twips.rs#L102), [alpha property](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/v0.7.1/core/src/display_object.rs#L654), and [Fixed8 conversion](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/v0.7.1/swf/src/types/fixed.rs#L73). For example, a7-frame shake with roll1 first stores0.55 then adds1, producing1.55; flash alpha is243/256 after one update and9/256 after19. The negative twentieth update remains tracked until removal21. These numerical contracts match Ruffle0.7.1; controlled Adobe Flash comparison remains open.
docs/fidelity.md:328:- `SwfGlowFilter` implements the pinned WGPU [glow branches](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/v0.7.1/render/wgpu/shaders/filter/glow.wgsl#L39-L75) and [fractional blur passes](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/v0.7.1/render/wgpu/src/filters/blur.rs#L183-L270). Horizontal then vertical repeats for each pass; each executed axis floors to8bit, widths cap at255, and an axis at width≤1 is skipped. A zero-pass/no-axis filter still composes against the original alpha. Strength saturates before the glow-color alpha is applied; knockout takes priority over composite-source. Padding follows the reference's pass-growth table and twip truncation. Ruffle explicitly calls this multi-pass bounds table approximate relative to Flash. Kernels remain in logical stage pixels; exact Stage/DPR scaling, pixel snapping and Adobe rasterization remain comparison gaps.
docs/fidelity.md:330:- Transform composition follows [signed Fixed8 wrapping multiplication and signed16-bit additive terms](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/v0.7.1/swf/src/types/color_transform.rs#L88-L116). The custom bitmap color shader unpremultiplies, transforms, saturates and premultiplies in the [default bitmap-shader order](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/v0.7.1/render/wgpu/shaders/bitmap.wgsl#L35-L51), preserving fully transparent pixels. Simple unfiltered alpha-only leaves retain Pixi's packed-alpha path; its byte quantization is not an Adobe pixel-parity claim. Existing collision providers and Script bounds remain separate from filter-expanded visual coverage.
docs/fidelity.md:332:- The development-only oracle independently composes byte images for all65 original parameter sets, the actual two-filter HUD stack, and13 controls covering every glow branch, zero passes/axes, inherited fade, post-glow tint, saturation and additive alpha. Browser comparisons read raw GPU premultiplied bytes directly. Pixi8.22's WebGL canvas extraction places those bytes into Canvas2D without unpremultiplying them; the shared fixture capture helper now converts extracted galleries to straight RGBA to avoid darkening the evidence twice. Existing galleries that read the live application canvas already receive the browser's normal conversion.
docs/fidelity.md:343:- A development-only gallery compares all73 native/mock silhouettes at the same scale and registration. Browser checks compare their actual alpha coverage, authored width and rotated/scaled contact; verify all five behavior designs; and place distinct guns and a behavior through the production editor with exported-radius checks. Existing projectile shoot-down and palette checks continue; the palette sampler now compares saturated paint so differently sized white rims do not skew the hue comparison. These checks measure the reconstruction against supplied vectors and do not establish complete Adobe Flash or game parity.
docs/fidelity.md:495:- The extended probe also observes saturating alpha limits −128…127.99609375, signed-twip position limits −107374182.4…107374182.35, NaN→0 and infinity saturation. `displayAlpha`/`displayPixel` preserve truncation, limits and stored-value feedback. This agrees with pinned [alpha conversion](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/89a7049965f3090e706265670df309a5128233ac/core/src/display_object.rs#L653-L665), [Fixed8 conversion](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/89a7049965f3090e706265670df309a5128233ac/swf/src/types/fixed.rs#L67-L75), [x/y setters](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/89a7049965f3090e706265670df309a5128233ac/core/src/avm2/globals/flash/display/display_object.rs#L329-L369) and [Twips conversion](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/89a7049965f3090e706265670df309a5128233ac/swf/src/types/twips.rs#L101-L104). Runtime alpha setters now use saturation; the preceding helper incorrectly wrapped 128 to −128 and −129 to 127. [ColorTransform composition](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/89a7049965f3090e706265670df309a5128233ac/swf/src/types/color_transform.rs#L75-L95) keeps its separate wrapping arithmetic and arithmetic-shift behavior.
docs/fidelity.md:497:- Verification: formatting, TypeScript, all 434 rule/parser tests with 5633 assertions and the production build pass. Alpha-setter saturation and parked-coordinate regressions both fail with their preceding implementations and pass after correction. All nine selected native/mock color, opacity, tank-art, pickup and geometric-contact browser cases pass. No original media or contours are committed. Retained pause/Info UI integration and complete game parity remain open.

Its title545 placement has no alpha transform (identity alpha1); `BubbleTanks3_fla/title_22.as` stops that wrapper on frame1 while its child544 retains the authored timeline. The caller still owns which submenu is open.
docs/fidelity.md:540:- `PauseMenu.as:167–251` stores local target coordinates and parks each row at its exit anchor. `_‑C7:405–448` enters settings in the authored order with strict updated-y<200 gates; `_‑Lz:857–895` enters hotkeys with updated-y<400 gates. Back and Locked independently share Pause’s gate. `_‑B9:1336–1346` and `_‑eE:845–854` retract only y, preserving literal0.93/0.07 and quantized assignments. `SettingsMotion` preserves these rules. On hotkey frame36, Pause first reaches398.8 and both dependent rows move immediately: Back543.85 and Locked539.35. Exact regressions distinguish that behavior from gating Locked through Back.

The supplied SWF supplies native morphs/text; mock painting uses the imported placements, procedural capsules/dividers and system glyphs. Mock leaf alpha applies the parent's signed8.8 multiplier before channel clamping and invalidates its stopped-frame cache on alpha changes, preserving translucent brightening above1. Exact contour, line and glyph pixels still differ.
